desc: In mid-1948 the Project SIGN staff at Wright Field completed a Top Secret document, in the standard military 'estimate of the situation' format, concluding that the objects under investigation were interplanetary in origin. It went up the chain to Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Hoyt Vandenberg, who rejected it on the grounds that it lacked proof and directed that copies be destroyed. No copy has ever surfaced. This board treats the Estimate as the single most consequential missing document of the twentieth century on this subject, and its status is stronger than folklore: the Condon Report — commissioned and paid for by the Air Force under contract 44620-67-C-0035 — states in Section V Chapter 2 that the estimate was prepared, that Vandenberg rejected it, and that copies were destroyed. Edward Ruppelt, the first Blue Book director, published the same account in 1956 from personal knowledge. Against this, Air Force spokesmen and members of Congress have at times asserted no such estimate ever existed. The conflict is itself the datum: the government's own contracted history records a document the government elsewhere denies. It also establishes, twenty years before the Bolender memo and forty-seven before the GAO records finding, that destruction was the standard disposition for adverse conclusions.
